variant-first.note: Set A captures four title-block facts (structural engineer, MEP engineer, architect of record, team name) that are all directly supported by the text layer and correctly bound to the project. Set B contains no claims at all, so it captures none of the available information. The claims in A are faithful with supporting quotes and no invented values, so A is clearly better despite B having no outright errors.

baseline-first.note: Set A contains no claims at all, so it captures none of the title-block information on the page. Set B extracts four role/identity facts (structural engineer, MEP engineer, architect of record, team name) that are all directly supported by the text layer and correctly bound to the project. The only minor quibble is that the team-name quote normalizes the case of 'TEAM CAPITOL DC', but the value is faithful. Set B is clearly better.

Set A captures the full revision table (five revisions with dates and descriptions), the drawing scale 3/8" = 1'-0" for both sections, and the lot number, all supported by the text layer. Set B omits the entire revision history, the scale, and the project/client information, which are prominent facts on the sheet, though its nine claims are otherwise accurate and it correctly adds the sheet title. Set A's only questionable item is binding 'U.S. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY SOLAR DECATHLON 2013' as a project name when it appears in the client block as two separate lines. Both sets contain redundant restatements of the grade/finished-floor elevations, but A's coverage of the title block and revision data is decisively more complete.

variant-first.note: Set B captures the revision table (marks 1–5 with dates and descriptions) and the section scales (3/8" = 1'-0" for C1/West and A1/East), all supported by the text layer and image, whereas Set A omits these and instead repeats the Grade Level and Finished Floor elevations four to five times with trivial variations. Set A's claims are all supported but heavily redundant, missing the revision history and scale information entirely. Set B's only defect is binding 'U.S. DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY SOLAR DECATHLON 2013' to 'Project name' when the sheet labels it CLIENT (the project is Borealis).

Both sets correctly capture the 2'-9 1/2" finished floor over 0'-0" grade and the room contents of the two sections, but both also invent a 2'-3 1/2" finished floor value that appears nowhere on the sheet. Set A additionally binds the 3/8"=1'-0" scales to the correct detail bubbles (A1 Living Room Section, C1 Section – Centre Module) and records the Centre/West Module adjacency and Living Room–Kitchen layout, all supported by the drawing. Set B instead adds misbound or vague claims (CENTRE MODULE location = grid bubble K, Mechanical Room location = "Building Section A302", "building section contains room" with unnamed entity, WEST MODULE location = West) that the sheet does not support as stated. Set A is therefore more faithful overall despite its duplicate claims.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same misread of the finished floor elevation as 2' - 3 1/2" where the sheet and text layer both read 2' - 9 1/2", and both repeat several claims. Set A adds unsupported bindings: CENTRE MODULE located at grid 'K' (quote does not support it), Mechanical Room located in 'Building Section A302' (A-302 is the sheet number, not a section), plus vague claims like 'building section contains room' and the tautology 'WEST MODULE location West'. Set B keeps the scale claims correctly tied to details A1 and C1 and the room/adjacency claims are supported by the section drawings, so it is the more faithful set despite considerable duplication.

variant-first.note: Set B captures the full revision table (dates and descriptions for revisions 1–5) and the sheet/lot data correctly, which Set A omits entirely, while both correctly record the C1/A1 section scales and the grade/finished-floor elevations. Set A's errors include a misread scale ('3/8 in/ft' instead of 3/8" = 1'-0"), two incomplete 'adjacent to' claims with no object, a Kitchen location claim whose quote ('KITCHEN') does not support it, and a misbound 'Building | section detail | A1'. Set B's errors are the invented 'Bedroom 4' adjacency pair, treating the client name as the project name, and a garbled C1 scale value ('3/8" 3/8" = 1'-0"'), plus two trivial room-layout claims. Overall B supplies more correct, document-supported facts with fewer substantive misreadings.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures the full revision table (five revisions with dates and descriptions), both section scales, and the grade/finished-floor elevations, which Set B omits almost entirely (no revision history at all). Set A does invent a 'Bedroom 4' entity twice and mislabels the client block as the project name, plus one garbled scale value for C1. Set B is cleaner on sheet identity (A-303, sheet title, lot number) and adds a reasonable Kitchen-in-C1 condition, but it drops the revisions and includes two incomplete 'spatial relationship | adjacent to' claims with no object, and one quote is reconstructed rather than verbatim. Overall A's broader correct coverage outweighs its few invented items.

variant-first.note: Set A captures several substantive facts that Set B omits entirely, notably the PV solar array, the 1/8" steel cable railing, the 1x4 T&G cedar siding/cladding details, and the A-511 Hardie installation reference, while both get the datum heights, solar envelope, APSE-20 tube model and 40-tube quantity right. Set B adds the door-swing note and the 1/4"=1'-0" scale, but it is padded with trivial identifier claims and three near-duplicate handrail claims and never mentions the PV array. Set A's weaknesses are two invented/vague bindings of 'PV SOLAR ARRAY' to a 'roof/upper structure' entity and one added 'relative to Grade Level' condition not in its quote; Set B's errors are mainly mislabeled 'height' attributes for the grade and finished-floor datums. Overall A is the more faithful and complete set.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are accurate on the shared core facts (solar envelope 18'-0", grade 0'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", 2 x APSE-20 / 40 tubes, cement fibre board siding, 2x4 cedar handrails, powdercoated steel flatbar railing posts, 1x4 T&G cedar cladding), with no misread or invented values in either. A is more complete on window/door marks (1.03, 1.05, 1.14, 1.13, 1.01, 1.02, 1.06) and captures the door-swing convention and the 1/4" scale, but repeats the handrail claim four times and restates the tube type. B adds the PV solar array, the 1/8" steel cable railing and the A-511 Hardie reference, but spends three claims on the PV array (two of them vague/trivial) and omits the scale and door-swing note. Overall coverage and fidelity are about equal.

Set A binds the core material and fastener facts correctly (3/4" x 5 1/2" plywood/reclaimed surface, 2" x 8" frame and joist, 3/8" x 4" hex through bolt incl. head type, 4x4 post, nails/screws, drawing scales), with a few misbound loose dimensions (1 1/4" as deck section height, 1 1/2" as decking thickness/joist width, 7 1/2" as decking support height, SLEVE as a threaded-rod connection) and one vague 'component 1' claim. Set B invents entities not on the sheet (bracket, top channel/bracket, footing overhang) for the 1 1/4", 3 3/4" and 4 1/4" dimensions, truncates the reclaimed wood surface value to 'X 5 1/2"', and misattributes 8'-0" to footing spacing in Detail C3. B does capture the FIRST FLR 2'-4" above GRADE LEVEL 0" relation that A omits, but it carries more misread, misbound and unsupported claims overall. Both sets contain substantial duplication of the same facts.

variant-first.note: Set B binds the through-bolt correctly as 3/8" diameter by 4" length, gives the full 3/4" x 5 1/2" plywood deck and reclaimed wood surface dimensions, and keeps the grade datum (0") and detail scales, all supported by the quoted labels. Set A truncates the reclaimed wood surface to "X 5 1/2"", invents an "overhang width (right)" attribute for the 4 1/4" footing dimension, and makes speculative bindings such as "bracket height 1 1/4"", "bracket width 3 3/4"" and "internal component height 3 1/2"", plus heavy duplication of the joist and footing claims. B is not perfect (e.g. "joist width 1 1/2"" and vague items like "component 1 height"), but it has fewer misbound or unsupported claims and covers the key material and fastener facts more faithfully.

Set A binds values to the correct detail regions (Module A total length 12'-3 3/4", center segment 7'-0", 3/8" through bolt, L3X3X1/4 angle) and keeps the C1/Module B and A1/Module A groupings largely consistent. Set B invents attributes (hole center height, gap to center, single block) and misbinds 2'-3 7/8" — an A1/Module A dimension — to Module B/Detail A, plus uses a truncated entity label ("MODULE B - P") and repeats several values. Both sets contain vague attribute names and duplicate claims, but A's duplicates are at least correctly located while B's include outright misbindings and unsupported properties.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds values to the sheet's actual named entities and details more faithfully, capturing the through-bolt diameter (3/8" THROUGH BOLT), the L3X3X1/4 angle, Module A total length 12'-3 3/4" and its 7'-0" center segment, and consistently tags Detail C1 vs A1. Set A invents components and attributes not on the sheet ("base block" hole center height, gap to center, width to center, "top connection", "right-side component"), duplicates several dimensions under conflicting labels, and misattributes 2'-3 7/8" (an A1/Module A dimension) to Module B and to a truncated "MODULE B - P" entity. Both sets contain vague "dimension" claims and duplicate values, but B's errors are mostly generic attribute wording while A's include outright misbinding and fabricated conditions. B therefore has more correct, better-bound claims and fewer serious errors.

variant-first.note: Set A binds dimensions to the correct detail/beam (e.g., 3'-7" and 6" opening height to Detail C4, 2'-1"/8"/9'-3" to Detail D5, 5'-1"/4'-6" to the grid 2 beam, 10'-0" to the grid 6 beam) and correctly reads W10X15 vs W8X13 sections. Set B repeatedly misassigns dimensions across details: ø 3" is attributed to B1 though it appears only with the W8X13 roof beams (C1/E6), 1'-3" and 1'-1" are bound to the wrong beams, 5'-0" and 5'-1" are shifted to the wrong grid beams, and 3'-1"/1'-8"/6"/10" are labeled as opening widths or edge distances when they are beam lengths, opening heights or opening widths. Set B also contains a garbled quote ("D 2,3,4,5 T.O. STEEL") and vague entities like "opening/spacing" and "beam opening group". Set A's main errors are two claims calling the 6" opening height a beam "depth" and one calling the 2" offset a "top flange width".
